events.title: Navy Establishes Coastal Stations
events.description: The U.S. Navy establishes 20 coastal stations to communicate with 24 wireless-equipped ships.

events.title: Modern Electrics Founded
events.description: Hugo Gernsback starts publishing Modern Electrics in New York, a key source for radio experimenters.

events.title: Junior Wireless Club Formed
events.description: The Junior Wireless Club, the first amateur radio organization, is formed in New York City.

events.title: Navy Skill Certificates
events.description: The Navy issues 447 certificates of skill in radio communication, mostly to amateur operators.

events.title: Anti-Amateur Bills Defeated
events.description: Amateurs successfully lobby against two Congressional bills that would have restricted their operations.

events.title: Radio Club of America
events.description: The Junior Wireless Club is renamed the Radio Club of America (R.C.A.).

events.title: Second Legislative Victory
events.description: A second attempt to restrict amateur radio through legislation is defeated by R.C.A. opposition.

events.title: Radio Act of 1912
events.description: President Taft signs the Radio Act of 1912, relegating amateurs to '200 meters and down'.

events.title: Initial Licensing Surge
events.description: In the first four months of the 1912 law, 1,185 amateur licenses are issued.

events.title: Growing Ham Population
events.description: By the end of 1913, the number of licensed amateur operators reaches nearly 2,000.

events.title: Radio Club of Hartford
events.description: The Radio Club of Hartford holds its first meeting; Hiram Percy Maxim is a key attendee.

events.title: ARRL Concept Presented
events.description: Maxim presents his plan for a national relay organization to the Radio Club of Hartford.

events.title: ARRL Founded
events.description: The American Radio Relay League is officially established to facilitate long-distance communication.

events.title: Amateur License Milestone
events.description: Licensed amateurs in the U.S. surpass 5,000, with over 10,000 total transmitters active.

events.title: Relay Routes Proven
events.description: The ARRL successfully demonstrates several reliable relay routes across the Northeast.

events.title: Network Expansion
events.description: The list of registered ARRL relay stations grows to over 200 across the U.S. and Canada.

events.title: First List of Stations
events.description: The Radio Club of Hartford publishes the first official list of amateur stations and routing tables.

events.title: ARRL Incorporation
events.description: Maxim and colleagues incorporate the ARRL as an independent entity separate from the Hartford club.

events.title: Expanding Directory
events.description: The second edition of the List of Amateur Stations is published, now containing 600 entries.

events.title: Creation of QST
events.description: The ARRL launches QST magazine to coordinate its growing membership and technical efforts.

events.title: Postcard QSL Idea
events.description: The idea of using postcards for reception reports (QSLs) is first suggested in QST.

events.title: Marconi Telephone Demo
events.description: The Marconi Wireless Telephone is demonstrated during a voyage to Boston.

events.title: ARRL Reorganization
events.description: The ARRL Board meets to reorganize post-WWI and plans a 'midget' issue of QST.

events.title: Receiving Ban Lifted
events.description: The U.S. Navy officially lifts the wartime ban on radio receiving for amateur operators.

events.title: Canada Resumes Operations
events.description: The ban on amateur radio is lifted in Canada under new proximity-based regulations.

events.title: QST Reopening Number
events.description: QST magazine returns to regular publication with a special 'Reopening Number'.

events.title: Navy Test Broadcasts
events.description: The Navy begins broadcasting test messages from station NAJ for amateur practice.

events.title: Hoffman QSL Postcard
events.description: Don Hoffman writes to QST about using postcards to report heard signals.

events.title: Draft Radio Bill
events.description: A new Congressional bill proposes replacing the 1912 law with a technical committee.

events.title: Transmitting Ban Lifted
events.description: The U.S. government finally lifts the wartime restriction on amateur radio transmitting.

events.title: Liberty Number
events.description: QST publishes the 'LIBERTY NUMBER,' celebrating the return of amateur radio freedoms.

events.title: Post-War Call Directory
events.description: The first post-war directory of amateur call signs is published, starting with the first district.

events.title: Armstrong Weak Signal Paper
events.description: Edwin Armstrong presents his paper on short-wavelength weak signal reception to the R.C.A.

events.title: Natural Radio Blackout
events.description: A natural blackout affects shorter wavelengths while 600-meter signals remain strong.

events.title: Superheterodyne Article
events.description: Armstrong's seminal article on the superheterodyne principle is published in QST.

events.title: Amateur CW Arrival
events.description: QST declares that amateur continuous wave (CW) telegraphy is now proven for relay work.

events.title: Solar Flare Blackout
events.description: A severe auroral display caused by a solar flare halts amateur message handling.

events.title: Colpitts Oscillator
events.description: The Colpitts oscillator is introduced to amateurs, aiding stable frequency control.

events.title: QSS Tests Announced
events.description: ARRL and the Bureau of Standards announce collaborative fading (QSS) tests.

events.title: QSS Tests Conclude
events.description: The first series of atmospheric fading tests conclude, providing valuable propagation data.

events.title: 8XK Regular Broadcasts
events.description: Frank Conrad's station 8XK begins regular music broadcasts, paving the way for KDKA.

events.title: QSS Test Report
events.description: The first part of the collaborative Bureau of Standards-ARRL fading report is published.

events.title: Transcontinental Relays
events.description: The ARRL conducts a series of record-setting coast-to-coast relay tests.

events.title: Reinartz Tuner Adoption
events.description: Hundreds of amateurs adopt the Reinartz tuner, revolutionizing CW reception.

events.title: Transcon Record Speed
events.description: A round-trip message between Hartford and Los Angeles sets a record of 6-1/2 minutes.

events.title: Heising Modulation Seminar
events.description: Raymond Heising presents a seminar on amplitude modulation theory at Columbia University.

events.title: The Chicago Plan
events.description: A cooperative model to resolve local interference is published and adopted in Chicago.

events.title: Reinartz Tuner Presentation
events.description: John Reinartz presents a tuner design optimized for CW that becomes highly popular.

events.title: Smith Cup to Chicago
events.description: The Smith Cup is established to recognize outstanding feats in amateur radio.

events.title: Spark vs. CW Contest
events.description: An on-air contest compares spark and CW effectiveness under noisy summer conditions.

events.title: Godley's UK Arrival
events.description: Paul Godley arrives in England to conduct the first ARRL transatlantic receiving tests.

events.title: 1BCG Antenna Done
events.description: Construction of the specialized antenna system for the 1BCG transatlantic station is completed.

events.title: Transpacific Reception
events.description: Clifford Dow in Hawaii successfully receives mainland amateur signals.

events.title: Godley Glasgow Arrival
events.description: Paul Godley arrives in Glasgow to set up his receiving station away from London's noise.

events.title: Ardrossan Signals
events.description: Godley successfully hears the first U.S. amateur signals from a station in Ardrossan, Scotland.

events.title: 1BCG Success
events.description: The high-power station 1BCG is heard by Godley, proving transatlantic amateur capability.

events.title: QST Success Banner
events.description: QST features a massive banner headline celebrating the success of transatlantic tests.

events.title: Smith Cup Award
events.description: The Chicago Executive Radio Council receives the Smith Cup for their cooperation model.

events.title: National Radio Conference
events.description: Herbert Hoover convenes the first conference to manage the crowded radio spectrum.

events.title: CW Surpasses Spark
events.description: For the first time, ARRL message traffic on CW exceeds traffic handled via spark.

events.title: Seefred CW Switch
events.description: The Seefred brothers switch to CW, quickly outperforming their old spark equipment.

events.title: Super-Regeneration Presentation
events.description: Edwin Armstrong presents his super-regenerative receiver design to the IRE.

events.title: Armstrong R.C.A. Demo
events.description: Armstrong demonstrates his super-regenerative receiver prototype to the R.C.A.

events.title: Armstrong Prototype R.C.A.
events.description: Edwin Armstrong demonstrates his super-regenerative prototype to the Radio Club of America.

events.title: Record Message Volume
events.description: Fred Schnell and others set new records for the number of messages handled in a month.

events.title: East Coast-Hawaii Relay
events.description: A message is relayed from Hartford to Hawaii and back in record time.

events.title: White Bill Congressional Hearing
events.description: ARRL President Maxim testifies before Congress to protect amateur radio status.

events.title: US Signals in China
events.description: Amateur signals are reported copied all the way to China by an operator on a ship.

events.title: Second Radio Conference
events.description: Hoover calls a second conference to manage the spectrum under existing 1912 laws.

events.title: 100 Meter CQ Party
events.description: ARRL holds a party to encourage exploration of the 100-meter wavelength.

events.title: Rochester Plan
events.description: ARRL promotes a voluntary time-sharing scheme to reduce interference for broadcast listeners.

events.title: Transpacific Tests
events.description: Vernice Bitz (6JD) becomes the first U.S. amateur station received in Australia.

events.title: MacMillan Arctic Expedition
events.description: The Bowdoin sets sail for the Arctic with operator Don Mix and amateur radio support.

events.title: Bowdoin Sails
events.description: The schooner Bowdoin departs with operator Don Mix (1TS) for a 14-month voyage.

events.title: WWV Standard Frequencies
events.description: WWV begins broadcasting standard frequencies to help hams calibrate their wave meters.

events.title: WNP News Receive Assignment
events.description: Station 1ZE is officially assigned to receive news dispatches from the Arctic expedition.

events.title: First WNP News Bulletin
events.description: Jack Barnsley (9BP) in British Columbia copies the first news from the MacMillan expedition.

events.title: Transpacific Test Milestone
events.description: Nearly 200 North American amateurs are successfully received in Australia during tests.

events.title: WNP Arctic Contacts
events.description: Amateurs establish regular contact with the frozen-in Bowdoin (WNP) in the Arctic.

events.title: Alaska-US First Contacts
events.description: The first recorded amateur contacts occur between Alaska and the continental United States.

events.title: Deloy's 100m Signal
events.description: Leon Deloy's 100-meter transmissions are immediately copied in the US, leading to a QSO.

events.title: Japan-US QSO
events.description: Charles York (7HG) makes the first two-way amateur contact across the Pacific with Japan.

events.title: First Inter-continental QSO
events.description: Fred Schnell (1MO) and Leon Deloy (8AB) complete the first two-way contact across the Atlantic.

events.title: Reinartz 115m Contact
events.description: John Reinartz successfully contacts Deloy on 115 meters, proving shortwave effectiveness.

events.title: 1MO-8AB Breakthrough
events.description: The 1MO-8AB contact proves that 100-meter waves are effective for global communication.

events.title: First US-UK QSO
events.description: Kenneth Warner and J.A. Partridge complete the first two-way contact between the US and UK.

events.title: Marconi-Maxim Exchange
events.description: Guglielmo Marconi replies to a message of respect sent by the ARRL via amateur radio.

events.title: Fourth Transatlantic Tests
events.description: The fourth ARRL transatlantic tests begin, aiming for two-way communication.

events.title: US-Holland First QSO
events.description: The first two-way amateur contact between the US and the Netherlands is achieved.

events.title: CQ Guideline Standard
events.description: Standard ARRL practices for efficient CQing are established to reduce interference.

events.title: Coolidge Arctic Greeting
events.description: A Christmas message from President Coolidge is successfully relayed to the Arctic expedition.

events.title: 4-Milliwatt Distance Record
events.description: Charles Maclurcan is heard 1,500 miles away while transmitting with only 4 milliwatts.

events.title: Transatlantic Log Deadline
events.description: Logs for the fourth transatlantic tests are due at ARRL headquarters.

events.title: NKF Shortwave Testing
events.description: The Naval Research Laboratory begins cooperative shortwave testing with amateur stations.

events.title: Tahiti Generator Search
events.description: Operators aboard the R.M.S. Tahiti search for a replacement generator in New Zealand.

events.title: SA-NZ Record Contact
events.description: Carlos Braggio in Argentina works New Zealand, setting a 6,400-mile distance record.

events.title: Braggio NZ Contact
events.description: Carlos Braggio remains in contact with New Zealand for over two hours in a record QSO.

events.title: Shortwave Bands Granted
events.description: The U.S. government officially grants amateurs access to new shortwave bands.

events.title: Esperanto Endorsement
events.description: ARRL endorses Esperanto as the international language for amateur radio communication.

events.title: Bowdoin Returns
events.description: The MacMillan expedition arrives back in Maine after nearly a year in the Arctic ice.

events.title: 3rd Radio Conference
events.description: The Third National Radio Conference discusses harmonically related amateur bands.

events.title: Radio Conference Reps
events.description: Eighty representatives from various radio services attend the 3rd National Radio Conference.

events.title: Abolition of Spark
events.description: The ARRL calls for the complete abolition of spark radio in favor of cleaner CW signals.

events.title: Spark Abolition Proposal
events.description: ARRL formally proposes the immediate abolition of amateur spark radio transmissions.

events.title: Ultra Short Wave Band
events.description: The Department of Commerce announces a new 3/4 meter 'ultra short wave' band for hams.

events.title: New SW Regs Effective
events.description: New regulations for amateur bands go into effect, marking a new era of shortwave use.

events.title: IARU Founded
events.description: The International Amateur Radio Union is formed in Paris to coordinate global amateur radio.

events.title: April in Paris (IARU)
events.description: The formation of the IARU in Paris marks a major milestone for international cooperation.

events.title: Washington Wireless Law
events.description: A new radio law is finally passed in Washington, establishing modern band allocations.

events.title: Third Party Traffic
events.description: The 1927 law introduces specific definitions and restrictions for third-party message traffic.

events.title: 1929-Type Station
events.description: A new generation of high-stability equipment, known as the '1929-type,' is introduced.

events.title: Perspectives on 1930
events.description: The ARRL reviews the state of amateur radio, celebrating its growth and technical maturity.
